ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, the line segment $AC$ is rotated $60^\circ$ counterclockwise around point $C$ to the line segment $CD$, where point $D$ falls exactly on side $AB$. Point $E$ is a point on side $BC$, and $AE$ and $DE$ are connected, with $\angle AEC=\angle BED=60^\circ$. Given that $AC=\sqrt{6}$ and $\angle BCD=15^\circ$, what is the length of $AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $CH\perp AE$ at point H,

$\because$ rotating line segment AC about point C by $60^\circ$ counterclockwise to line segment CD,

$\therefore AC= CD$, $\angle ACD=60^\circ$,

$\therefore \triangle ACD$ is an equilateral triangle, thus $\angle CAD=\angle CDA=60^\circ$, $AD=AC=CD$,

$\because \angle BCD=15^\circ$, $\angle AEC=\angle BED=60^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle EAD=180^\circ-\angle CDA-\angle AQD=180^\circ-\angle CEA-\angle CQE=\angle ECQ=15^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle CAH=\angle CAD-\angle EAD =45^\circ$,

$\because AC= \sqrt{6}$, $\angle CAH=45^\circ$, $CH\perp AE$,

$\therefore CH=AH= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AC= \sqrt{3}$,

$\because \angle CEH=60^\circ$,

$\therefore EH= \frac{CH}{\tan 60^\circ}=1$,

$\therefore AE= AH+ EH= \sqrt{3}+1=\boxed{\sqrt{3}+1}$;

In Figure 1, A, D, B are on the same straight line, and D lies on AB; C is above, and E lies on BC; AC, BC, AB, AE, CD, DE are connected, and AE and CD intersect inside the triangle. Reasoning: Let the intersection point of AE and CD be Q. From the meaning of the problem, line segment AC is rotated counterclockwise by 60° around C to obtain CD, so AC=CD, and ∠ACD=60°. Therefore △ACD is an equilateral triangle, ∠CAD=∠CDA=60°, and AD=AC=CD=√6. Because Q is on CD, A,D,B are collinear, and Q is on AE, in △ADQ, ∠EAD=∠QAD=180°−∠CDA−∠AQD=180°−60°−∠AQD. Also because ∠AQD and ∠CQE are vertical angles, ∠AQD=∠CQE; and Q is on AE, ∠CEA=60°, so ∠CEQ=60°. In △CEQ, ∠ECQ=180°−∠CEQ−∠CQE=180°−60°−∠CQE. Therefore ∠EAD=∠ECQ. Since E is on BC, CE and CB are collinear, so ∠ECQ=∠BCD=15°, hence ∠EAD=15°. Thus ∠CAE=∠CAD−∠EAD=60°−15°=45°. Draw CH⊥AE, with foot H. Then in right triangle ACH, AC=√6, ∠CAH=45°, so AH=CH=AC·√2/2=√3. Also H is on AE, ∠CEH=∠CEA=60°; in right triangle CEH, tan60°=CH/EH, so EH=CH/tan60°=√3/√3=1. Therefore AE=AH+EH=√3+1.
